verdict.rationale: Kimi documents an official terminal CLI. You run `kimi`, log in with `/login`, and the agent can read code, edit files, execute commands, search the web and complete development tasks on its own. It also exposes an ACP protocol so other editors can connect. A community user corroborates the Kimi CLI by name, preferring it over OpenCode. Missing for 10: documented installation steps and command reference, and evidence of a non-interactive/scriptable (headless) mode for automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Chat with AI in the terminal, letting it read code, edit files, execute commands, search the web, and autonomously complete development tasks.
run `kimi` in the terminal to start; on first use, log in to the Kimi Code platform with the `/login` command to complete the connection
Other editors such as JetBrains and Zed can connect via CLI's ACP protocol.
using OpenCode instead of the Kimi CLI really hurt performance
